present.name: Arty Wilmot

untold.label: 门厅里的编辑
untold.use: Private until introduced: appearance only; apply person, then called.name and say token.

present.wants: Guard access to the Globe clippings morgue and enjoy the little power of saying no.
present.fears: Looking weak in front of the newsroom if he caves too easily.
present.hides: He is not professionally skilled at social resistance — Regular difficulty social skills can move him; he just starts unhelpful by policy.
present.voice: Pompous, clipped, editorial. Loves denying 'the general public'.
mask: 语气拿腔作势，句子切得短，爱用报馆行话；开口便强调规矩与「公众」，对陌生人一律以规条相待，必要时才肯松口。
in exchange: 找馆长？馆长今天不见客。资料室归我管，你先说明来意。→ 这里是编辑部，不是阅览室。你要查什么，先报上名目，我再看合不合规矩。
上午十一点前收稿最多，别挑那时候来。→ 十一点前后送来，我就得先应付稿子。你要来，下午两点以后安静些，我还能腾出手。
我不是不给你看，规矩摆在这儿，谁来都一样。→ 规矩就是规矩，放你进去，明天全城的人都来翻旧报。你总得让我有个说得过去的由头。

personality.description: Arty Wilmot is a gatekeeper by instinct and policy, treating the Globe clippings morgue as his own fiefdom and savoring the small authority of telling people no. His fear is not exposure but appearing weak before the newsroom, which makes him guard his refusals long after the practical reason for them has faded. In practice he is far less formidable than he performs — regular social pressure can move him, and he resists by default posture rather than deep conviction, so a determined or well-judged approach tends to find the man behind the clipped, editorial bluster.

present.keeper_note: Use Charm / Intimidate / Persuade / Fast Talk as appropriate to the approach. Pushed failures escalate (backup muscle, offence, ejection).

present.name: Ruth Blake

untold.label: 剪报间的女职员
untold.use: Private until introduced: appearance only; apply person, then called.name and say token.

present.wants: Do her job in the clippings basement and be treated like a person.
present.fears: Getting in trouble with Arty for letting strangers linger.
present.hides: Friendly investigators learn the 1878 fire cutoff without a roll — the information is color, not the critical clue.
present.voice: Quiet, practical, basement-warm. Speaks in asides while filing.
mask: 说话轻，句子平常，一边翻卷一边答话；不摆架子也不寒暄，问到为难处就压低声音，把话岔到手上的活儿上去。
in exchange: 劳驾，请问这儿能查旧报纸吗？ → 能查。放着的那几摞别动，我给你取。你要哪一年的，说一声就行，我手边正好理到一半。
那你平时都在这儿待着？一整天见不着几个人吧。 → 是没什么人下来。楼上热闹，地下室安静，倒也合适我。你要坐就坐那边，别挡着道，我一会儿还得搬两箱上去。
听说这房子以前出过事，你在报馆这么久，就没听过什么？ → 旧报纸上什么都有，真真假假我也分不清。我在这儿管的是剪报，上面让留什么就留什么，旁的不好多说。你要查，就查，别让上头瞧见我陪人闲聊。

personality.description: Ruth Blake takes quiet, practical pride in doing her job well and in being treated like a person rather than furniture; she is helpful staff by disposition, warming to friendly investigators who take her seriously and offering plain, unguarded help within the bounds of her work. Her judgment is cautious and self-protective where authority is concerned, since she fears getting in trouble with Arty for letting strangers linger, so she balances small kindnesses against the risk of drawing attention. She keeps her voice low and basement-warm, furnishing context and small asides as she files more readily than she volunteers anything that could land her in trouble.

present.keeper_note: Escort into the morgue after Arty relents. Flirting/friendship yields the fire cutoff remark.
